translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: Let’s settle up, ferryman. I wanna know exactly what you owe me so we don’t keep bickering about it.

translation.speaker: Charon
translation.text: Fine, Hermes, let’s do the math. Better to get it straight and avoid the hassle.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: I got you an anchor. Cost me five drachmas.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: Swear to Hades, I paid five for it. Plus a rudder pin for two obols.

translation.speaker: Charon
translation.text: Alright, put down five drachmas and two obols.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: And a needle for the sail. I shelled out five obols for that.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: Then there’s wax to patch up the leaks in your lousy boat, plus nails and some rope for the rigging. Two drachmas for the whole lot.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: That’s everything, unless we missed something in the tally. So, when are you gonna pay me back?

translation.speaker: Charon
translation.text: Can’t do it now, Hermes. But if a plague or a war sends a big batch down here, I’ll make enough to cover it—maybe fudge the fares a little.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: So I’m just supposed to sit here praying for disaster so I can get my money?

translation.speaker: Charon
translation.text: No other way, Hermes. Look around—hardly anyone’s showing up. It’s peacetime.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: Guess that’s better, even if it means waiting on you to pay up. But man, Charon, you remember the old-timers? They’d roll in tough as nails, covered in blood, most of ‘em wounded. Now? It’s some guy poisoned by his kid or his wife, or some softie who ate and drank himself to death—swollen belly, weak legs, pale as ghosts. Nothing like the old crowd. And most of ‘em are down here ‘cause they got greedy, scheming against each other.

translation.speaker: Charon
translation.text: Well, money’s worth dying for, apparently.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: Exactly. So don’t think I’m outta line hounding you for what you owe me.

thinking: I’ve leaned into the sitcom register hard here, aiming for a Seinfeld-esque vibe with Hermes as the perpetually exasperated George Costanza type, griping about every little expense, and Charon as the put-upon DMV clerk who’s just trying to keep things moving. The dialogue is punchy and quick, with short sentences and a conversational flow that feels like a 90s TV argument over a bar tab. I’ve kept the financial details (drachmas, obols) intact for specificity and humor—it’s funnier to hear Hermes itemize every petty cost. The cultural jab at modern shades being weak and greedy compared to the heroic old-timers is played up as a nostalgic rant, fitting Hermes’ aggrieved tone. I avoided archaisms entirely, using ‘pay me back’ and ‘settle up’ for natural phrasing. The recurring theme of death-by-greed is highlighted in Hermes’ final rant to tie into the broader Cynic humor of the series.
key_terms: πορθμεῖα (porthmeia): translated as 'fares' for Charon’s ferry fee.
δραχμή (drachma) and ὀβολός (obol): kept as is for specificity and humor in the itemized list.
uncertainties: Decided to keep ‘drachmas’ and ‘obols’ untranslated for comedic effect—might be unfamiliar to some audiences but context should clarify.
Interpreted Hermes’ tone in the final line as sarcastic agreement with Charon’s comment on money, though it could also be read as bitter resignation.
